text: What is distinctive of Paul Horwich's minimalism about truth?
choices: Truth is a substantive relation of correspondence between a proposition and its truthmaker.
Truth is warranted assertibility under the idealized epistemic conditions available to an ideal inquirer.
The set of all instances of the equivalence schema 'the proposition that p is true iff p' exhausts the nature of truth.
Truth is realized by correspondence in the physical domain and by superassertibility in the moral domain.
explanation: Horwich's minimalism takes the (unproblematic) instances of the equivalence schema, applied to propositions, to say everything there is to say about truth: there is a property of truth, but a minimal, non-explanatory one. Option 0 is correspondence; option 1 is Dummettian anti-realism; option 3 is truth pluralism. Minimalism also differs from Quine's disquotationalism, which takes sentences rather than propositions as the bearers of truth.
